note.question: Can a flexible platform-based ride-hailing incumbent outperform a capacity-owning robotaxi entrant, and when does AV entry improve or reduce customer and social welfare?
note.overview: A vertically integrated autonomous-vehicle entrant commits capacity, the incumbent ride-hailing platform sets driver revenue share, both firms compete in prices, and drivers and consumers choose participation. The paper explicitly solves the resulting multistage subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium.

models.method: The authors formulate monopoly and postentry games, solve driver and consumer market clearing, work backward through firm prices, revenue sharing and AV capacity, compare equilibrium market structure and welfare, and use numerical analysis for parameter regions without compact closed forms.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Before entry, the RH platform sets driver revenue share and ride price, followed by driver and consumer participation. Postentry, the AV firm first chooses fleet capacity K; the RH firm then chooses revenue share α; both firms simultaneously set prices; consumers choose AV, RH, or no ride and drivers choose whether to supply RH service. The AV entrant owns capacity and commits it before prices. The RH firm induces rather than owns vehicle supply, using revenue share to attract drivers.
